  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are
not listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no
action may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items
needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not
subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual
consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so
declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the
Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The
Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public
speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under

Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing
KManisco@malibucity.org.

for the deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In

meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext.
229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to
ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing
agenda was posted in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 29th day of January
2024 at 4:00 p.m.

Subject:  Environmental Sustainability Program

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Discuss and approve the environmental sustainability
public service announcements; and 2) Select three Commissioners to record the public
service announcements.

DISCUSSION: At the June 26, 2023 Regular meeting, Council approved an assignment
for the Youth Commission to work with the Community Services Department to create a
program to promote environmental sustainability.

At the January 11, 2024 Special meeting, the Commission approved filming and posting
public service announcements (PSA) related to environmental sustainability. The
Commission would work with staff to post the videos on the City’s website and social
media platforms during Earth Month, April 2024.

To fulfill the assignment, staff recommends the Commission approve the three PSA
scripts (Attachment). The PSAs highlight,

   Clean Water Initiatives
   Earth Hour
   Solid and Organic Waste Recycling

In addition to approving the PSAs, the Commission is asked to nominate three
Commissioners to record and submit the video to staff.

ATTACHMENTS: Draft Environmental Sustainability Public Service Announcements

  Page 1 of 1  Agenda Item # 4.A.
 Draft Environmental Sustainability Public Service Announcements
2023-24 Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission

PSA #1
April is Earth Month, a time to celebrate our planet and take action to protect it.
The Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission encourages you to attend a free
Organics Recycling Training on April 17 coordinated by the City of Malibu
Environment Sustainability Department. Organic waste, such as food scraps,
emits short-lived climate pollutants. Reducing these pollutants will have the fastest
impact on the climate crisis. All Malibu residents receive a free kitchen collection
bin after attending the training. Visit MalibuCity.org/Organics for more information.

PSA #2
The Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission encourages all Malibu residents
to protect our blue backyards and underwater neighbors from urban runoff. Malibu
is home to the largest Area of Special Biological Significance where any kind of
non-stormwater runoff is prohibited. You can help by preventing pollution to our
beaches from the following sources: runoff from washing your car, pet waste, lawn
chemicals, construction debris, and pool or water feature drainage. Visit
MalibuCity.org/Environmental/EnviroPrograms for more information.
PSA #3
Join the Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission in celebration of Earth Hour
on Saturday, March 23, at 8:30 PM. We encourage you to switch off your lights
and give an hour to the Earth, to show support for our planet. Visit EarthHour.org
for more information.

Guidelines
   Still background
   Appropriate attire
   Landscape orientation (not portrait/vertical)
   Maximum length 15 seconds
   Include your first name only and state you are a member of the Youth
  Commission

Date prepared:  January 25, 2024  Meeting date: February 1, 2024

Subject:  Arts Program

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Discuss ideas for the 2024 Arts Program.

DISCUSSION: At the June 26, 2023 Regular meeting, Council approved an assignment
for the Youth Commission to coordinate an event or program that may include spoken
word, music, dance, film, or visual art.

The Commission has organized an arts or music program since 2015 including the Teen
Film Festival, Battle of the Bands, and Teen Music and Art Festival. Since 2018, the
Commission has partnered with the Community Services Department to co-host the
Student Art Exhibit including marketing opportunities, artist recruitment, and other event
components such as art demonstrations.

The Commission is asked to discuss ideas for the 2024 Arts Program, including topics of
interest, community partners, potential dates, and locations.
